summary:
# NOTES: TWO BOOKS

## BOOK 1: PRIDE AND HIS PRISONERS (A. L. O. E.)

### Ch I. The Haunted Dwelling
- Spring Sabbath, Somersetshire. Nettleby Tower on hill: Norman robber-hold, Commonwealth siege marks, moat dry, portcullis rusted.
- Ruin caused by lawsuit and family dissension. Property held by Mr. Auger (owner, didn't live there).
- Last Mr. Bardon (Hugh) disinherited only son Timon for marrying farmer's daughter (30+ yrs back). Timon now Dr. Bardon in needy cottage in sight of tower.
- Old woman guide; tower "haunted" by spirits of Pride and Intemperance (personified, not ghosts).
- Dialogue: Intemperance (wild red-meteor eyes) vs Pride (taller, darker, deeper voice).
  - Pride's three fermentations: vinous (high spirit), acid (sour brooding), last stage (hating/hated, self-worship, rebellion, unbelief).
  - Pride says he hardened Hugh Bardon's soul; Intemperance drives gin-palace victims.
  - Pride enters church unseen; "my banner over the Christian's tomb."
  - Pride: "As David with his sling to Goliath, so to Pride is the Spirit of the Gospel."
  - Pride: "I dig the deep hidden pit-fall"; disguises: "pardonable weakness," "natural instinct," "generous virtue."
  - Pastor's daughter Ida Aumerle (soft dark eye) resists; Pride wants to enslave her since childhood.
- Footnote: lady to pastor "What a beautiful sermon"; pastor: "The devil told me the very same thing."

### Ch II. Resisted, Yet Returning
- Ida (Aumerle), at 12 lost mother; younger sister Mabel (clever, impulsive, fearless).
- Ida loved mirror, dress, braiding hair. Then one night reading Bible, tears, prayer: "birthday of a soul." Pride lost beauty-hold.
- Ida's humility: calls self "a sinner... saved only by mercy." Refuses spiritual pride.
- ~2 years later (age 18), at uncle Augustine Aumerle's home Aspendale: Reginald, Earl of Dashleigh (Augustine's college friend) proposed; Ida refused (he wears "my chain openly"); returned to father.
- Dashleigh, piqued, married cousin Annabella (Ida's cousin) soon after.
- Father Lawrence Aumerle remarried Mrs. Barbara Aumerle (née Lambert), capable, practical, "common sense," assisted in parish machinery.
- Ida dethroned: "second where she had been first." Pride's "independent state" strategy: represents step-mother's advice as interference.
- Pride's disguise for spiritual pride/self-will: "sensitiveness."

### Ch III. Snares
- Pastor Lawrence and Mrs. Aumerle walk to church. Mrs. Aumerle condemned Ida's anthem (trio of 3 girls); Ida gave up music choir.
- Lawrence Aumerle: vicar of Ayrley; prosperous, self-satisfied until wife died (saintly death); humbled.
- Augustine Aumerle: handsome, brilliant, Cambridge honours, sceptic, German philosophy, "pride of intellect." Pride: "I am leading him... to become one [sceptic]."
- Timon Bardon (long white hair) glances at tower.
- Pride's warning: "pride of poverty" also exists.
- Narrator: prologue as dialogue; asks reader to check if he is a prisoner of Pride.

### Ch IV. A Glance into the Cottage
- Mill Cottage: stone, two storeys, iron knocker, verandah apology. Polyanthus garden.
- Parlour: deal table, tidies on chairs, watercolour flowers, green guitar-box, pink ribbon, tiny mirror, miniatures, china figures (one missing arm, one head).
- Cecilia Bardon: 30–40, sallow, light hair, grey eyes; pride = dress; fawn-coloured kid boots; no fire 1 Apr–Nov; curtain/subscription/boots dilemma—boots won.
- Dr. Timon Bardon: dark flashing eyes, beetling brows, white mane, drawn-down mouth, leonine; reads theology.
- Dislikes countess's wedding cards on mirror-rack; "Only one year and ten months since Annabella married."
- Bardon's axiom: "It's the fool that gets on in the world."
- Mabel's hyacinths gift from doctor; Ida and Mabel bring crimson curtain. Doctor annoyed at obligation.
- Ida invites Cecilia and father to Dashleigh Hall (Annabella's message).
- Dispute: "Mill Cottage" (Bardon) vs "Milton Cottage" (Cecilia, pretentious).
- Bardon's mental "glass": small for others' deeds, big for his own (Mabel's observation).

### Ch V. Both Sides
- Mabel: "The world may be divided into two classes—those made of porcelain, and those of crockery." Mrs Aumerle = crockery.
- Ida: "It is our appointed trial."
- Ida's farm-boys class (Saturday evening); conflict with mothers' meeting in school-room.
- Mrs Aumerle scolds girls for crossing fields after sunset; Mabel's cheek flushes.
- Pride whispers to Ida.
- Mrs Aumerle: "your father's daughter teaching... hulking farm lads"; she will teach lads herself; Ida gets mothers' meeting. Ida reluctant.
- Mrs Aumerle quotes 1 Peter 5:5 / James 4:6 ("God resisteth the proud").

### Ch VI. The Visit to the Hall
- Cecilia obsesses over the visit. Father yields after two days.
- Pelton (6 miles) clarence refused; farmer's donkey-chaise hired.
- Cecilia's silk dress, dusty; boots; donkey stubborn.
- Lodge-keeper Mills; "Dr. and Miss Bardon, of Milton Cottage."
- Dashleigh Hall: Bardon: "Mere gingerbread!"
- Annabella: small (Titania), vivacious dark eyes, irregular profile, ink stain, writing romance.
- Annabella's warm greeting; "I will conquer the old lion." Gets Bardon's Venice Sumach slip.
- Cecilia: "She has not a particle of pride!"

### Ch VII. A Misadventure
- Annabella's background: orphaned, grandmother's darling. Ambition: pen name "Egeria" in monthly periodical.
- Dashleigh proposed (smarting from Ida's refusal); Annabella dazzled by coronet.
- Marriage: Pride whispers discord to each—Dashleigh: wife vulgar; Annabella: husband weak, "accident of birth."
- Dashleigh: "Griselda" comparison; Annabella rebels.
- Dashleigh's pride: 12th Earl; nervous, poor horseman, weak nerves.
- Donkey brays, Dashleigh thrown; orders servants: "Tell Mills never again..."
- Duke of Montleroy invited to luncheon; covers laid for four.
- Dashleigh: "Can't you manage some way of getting rid of these miserable Bardons?" overheard by Bardon.
- Bardon's blistering speech: "I retort back the opprobrious term!"; "this shall be the last" visit.
- Annabella weeps; Pride triumphant.

### Ch VIII. A Brother's Effort
- Vicar Lawrence & Augustine in study; Augustine: Bible "mere cant"; reason vs revelation; Lawrence reads Psalm 131; "meek will he guide."
- Augustine: origin of sin; Lawrence: "the true stumbling-block... is our pride."
- Augustine: Ida "too good"; Lawrence: "spiritual experience... ignorance of holiness."
- Pride: "Nail him with that difficulty."
- Augustine quits study; plays Tennyson with nieces; Lawrence prays on knees.

### Ch IX. Disappointment
- Annabella revises proofs of "Egeria" first romance, volume in violet and gold.
- Earl objects to writing as countess; "Tyrant!" (Pride whispers).
- Earl: "private circulation" concession; Annabella refuses ("begging-box").
- Earl forbids sale: "My dignity is connected with my own."
- Annabella writes "The Precipice and the Peer": Swiss mountain, Dashleigh's vertigo, boa from wife, Albert Smith reference. Intent: revenge, to publish; plans to ask magazine to print.

### Ch X. On the Watch
- Ida & Mabel in arbour (honeysuckle, clematis). Mabel: "Uncle says Ida has no fault except being too good."
- Ida: "I threw away my ladder long ago... every round was broken." Golden cord of faith.
- Prayer critique: "The dearest idol I have known..." (Keble hymn quoted).
- Ida compares: man of business refusing books; keeper of castle.
- Mabel's head on Ida's bosom; Pride baffled.

### Ch XI. The Quarrel
- Earl & Annabella in boudoir. Augustine invited them to balloon ascent at Aspendale (Verdon the æronaut, the Eaglet). Earl doubts etiquette; Annabella teases ("boa").
- Earl reads magazine; finds "The Precipice and the Peer" in her drawer; tears it, tramples it.
- "Leave the room, insolent girl!" Duke of Montleroy witnesses.
- Annabella orders Bates: carriage, "I shall sleep at the vicarage to-night."
- Servants' gossip: butler, Bates ("She has a spirit of her own").
- Annabella vows never to yield.

### Ch XII. The Unexpected Guest
- Evening at vicarage: Bardon brings crystallised pebble; chess with Mrs Aumerle.
- Cecilia sings "Bel raggio lusinghier," overdone.
- Mabel asks to go in balloon; Mrs Aumerle: "That's pride."
- Augustine invites Bardon, Cecilia, and Earl to ascent. Bardon: "I would sit down with farmer—ploughboy—pauper, but not... Reginald Earl of Dashleigh."
- Mabel sees red liveries: Dashleigh carriage.
- Annabella arrives haggard; Lawrence takes her to study. Ida asked to share room with Mabel.
- Bardon: "I'd rather have him for my enemy than my friend!"

### Ch XIII. The Friend's Mission
- Mrs Aumerle: "a young wife does wrong... leaving home."
- Mabel defends Annabella; Mrs A: "A child of fifteen is no judge."
- Narrator: Mabel's "feelers" comparison; Mrs A had no sensitivity.
- Augustine's mission: Earl demands Annabella apologize and return that day.
- Annabella: "Forgiveness to the injured doth belong, / He never pardons who hath done the wrong."
- Lawrence says she needs a doctor; Bardon called.

### Ch XIV. A Fatal Step
- Annabella confides; Bardon: "What a fool he was to quarrel with one who has him so completely at her mercy!"
- Bardon: write the paper again, publish it: "It would be revenge!" Annabella agrees.
- Bardon tells Aumerles he gave "something to compose."
- Ida rebuffed at door: "I wish to be alone!"
- Annabella's letters: (1) "The Precipice and the Peer" to magazine editor; (2) to London publisher authorising name "Countess of Dashleigh" on title page.
- Bates to post letters; Ida tempted to intervene, withheld.
- Annabella regrets; Mabel offers to call back Bates; Annabella says "No"—"too late."

### Ch XV. The Deserted Home
- Earl lonely; Pride-induced isolation; self-reproach.
- Magazine: "Now in the press. THE FAIRY LAKE: A Romance. By the COUNTESS OF DASHLEIGH."
- Earl reads "The Precipice and the Peer" — wounded.
- Lawrence's letter to earl (pleads for Annabella).
- Earl writes Augustine: "reserve me a place in the car... 12th."

### Ch XVI. Pleading
- Ida pleads with Annabella: "Pride... barring against you a husband's heart."
- Annabella: "I cannot cringe beneath the rod."
- Mrs Aumerle enters; rebukes Annabella; reveals Lawrence wrote to earl disapproving.
- Annabella leaves for Mill Cottage (Bardons). Bates to follow.
- Ida: "It was your coming that changed all!"

### Ch XVII. Conscience Asleep
- Narrator: conscience differences; Bardon's religion has no effect on temper.
- Bardon walks six miles to Pelton, library: magazine sold out ("a hit on one of the leading men").
- Bardon sees Cecilia; declines lunch.

### Ch XVIII. The Magazine
- Baker's boy and page with magazine; Bardon fails to buy it.
- Bardon visits Mrs. Clayton (blind widow); reads article: "Capital! capital!"
- Bardon reads Times: death of Mr. Auger of Nettleby Tower. Gloats.
- Bardon: "six feet of earth" for Auger.
- Annabella now at Mill Cottage; Cecilia sews drugget; Bates disdains.
- Cecilia: "not a particle of pride."

### Ch XIX. Expectation
- Rumour: Dashleigh to ascend in the Eaglet.
- Annabella gloomy; won't eat.
- Bardon resolves to attend ascent to see Dashleigh humiliated.
- Mabel gets Lawrence's permission ("ask your mother's opinion"); Mrs A: "I... put an extinguisher" (Mabel's "opinion" vs "consent" distinction).
- Ida dislikes but yields; Ida's reasons = pride.

### Ch XX. A Sunny Morn
- 12 May: Mabel slips out early; meets uncle Augustine on Black Prince (gig) at dawn.
- Augustine: Dr. Bardon's sneer; "Is that Bardon's cottage?" "Lion and bear."
- Verdon: small, sharp features, keen grey eyes.
- Aspendale Lodge (wooded hill, meadow of daisies and buttercups).
- Bardon's sarcastic remarks ("swollen pride").
- Crowd: labourers, shopboys, farmers' wives.
- Earl arrives in red-liveried chariot, pale as corpse, walks with Augustine.

### Ch XXI. The Ascent
- Narrator: guillotine analogy; earl's horror of heights; "I must, I must."
- Earl drinks wine.
- Earl panics; seizes car; crowd cries "Let go!" — balloon launches.
- Verdon: "Merciful Heaven! they are lost!" Signal given too soon; valve issue.
- Bardon: "How shall I tell this to Annabella?"

### Ch XXII. In the Clouds
- Mabel delighted; Augustine pale.
- Augustine pulls valve rope; balloon enters cloud; rope snapped; valve broken.
- Panorama: sea of cloud; Dashleigh Hall like toy.
- Earl faints after whirlwind; wine cork explosion.

### Ch XXIII. Regrets
- Ida's qualms: she ought to have stopped Mabel.
- Ida tells Lawrence she wants to visit Annabella.
- Bardon gallops up: "Lost! lost!"
- "Augustine Aumerle... Mabel... the Earl of Dashleigh."
- Balloon sighted, then vanishes.
- Annabella: "you who led me to this abyss... never let me behold you again!"

### Ch XXIV. Soaring Above Pride
- Sunset; earl calm, believes they'll die ("death is a great preacher"); text: Isaiah 2:17.
- Gas can't be released; knife fails.
- Mabel writes farewell to father & Ida; apology to Mrs A; drops letter.
- Earl gives Annabella's gift pocketbook (gold shield, coronet, two words in pencil) — drops into abyss.
- Evening: Augustine declines to pray; earl leads Litany; "Lord, deliver us!"

### Ch XXV. A Broken Chain
- Annabella remorseful; idealises earl.
- Ida's prayer; Bible gift from Mabel.
- Mrs Aumerle: confident Augustine will land safely.
- Ida confesses to Mrs A that she failed to stop Mabel; Mrs A embraces her: "I believe there were faults on both sides!"
- Pride flees: "chain of his captive was broken."

### Ch XXVI. The Awful Crisis
- Night: Augustine's reflection on pride of intellect; "As well might I fling myself from this car."
- Dawn: balloon less inflated; ballast thrown; splash.
- Descent over Channel to sea; instruments and basket dropped.
- Augustine cuts ropes; car rebounds, dips in sea; earl and Mabel bail with hat and beaver.
- Balloon released, flies away.
- Drift all day; thirst; sail spotted (earl: "God be praised!"); rescue by fishing smack.

### Ch XXVII. Tidings
- Night of anguish at vicarage.
- Annabella's publisher letter: cancel edition; she pays losses.
- Telegram from Augustine, from Cliff Cottage, B——, Devon: "Safe, thank God! ... earl... brain fever... Dr. G—— and a nurse. —A. A."
- Annabella insists on going; Lawrence escorts; Ida sent with Mabel's parcel (Bible). Mrs A orders.
- Mrs A's soliloquy: "common sense... most uncommon."
- Mabel's letter found by farmer; Mrs A softened ("let bygones be bygones").

### Ch XXVIII. The Wheel Turns
- Bardon's dinner rage; Cecilia's tartlets.
- Bardon sullen; sealed black-bordered letter from executors: Auger's will leaves Nettleby Tower to Timon Bardon, plus compensation for lawsuit.
- Bardon humbled; Cecilia happy.
- Train; station official: nobleman picked up from sea by fishing smack; chaise sent for doctor.
- Night walk on chalky road; gorge; "valley of the shadow of death."
- Fisherman's shingle cottage by the sea; Mabel in father's arms.

### Ch XXIX. Two Words
- Dr. G—— blocks Annabella from sick-room (thinks she's the authoress).
- Night in cramped fisherman's hovel; earl feverish, delirious.
- Augustine & Lawrence on shore: Augustine: "I have, then, lived an age in the last forty hours." Confesses faith; Lawrence rejoices.
- Earl's pocketbook returned by a farmer (stained, found near Mabel's letter); Ida finds pencilled "forgiveness" and "peace."
- Annabella goes in; reconciliation with husband in fisherman's hut.

### Ch XXX. The Spirit Laid
- July; earl in Annabella's boudoir, reading "The Fairy Lake"; Annabella now submits.
- Earl proposes visit to Bardons: "wish the old man and his daughter joy."
- Tour of Nettleby Tower: Bardon guides; Cecilia's pride in showing; Mrs A notes rubbish.
- Ida and Mabel imagine knights; Bardon glowers at "Dashleigh."
- Augustine on haunting: "such spirits are wont to haunt new houses as well."
- Dashleigh's carriage arrives; Bardon shamed; Dashleigh extends hand; Bardon wrings it; enmity laid.
- Narrator's closing: Pride is life-long; exhortation to clip soaring wing of the Eaglet; closing poem on pride.

---

## BOOK 2: THE DATCHET DIAMONDS (Richard Marsh)

### Ch I. Two Men and a Maid
- Brighton. Waltz at the Dome (Masonic Ball) danced with Mr. Lawrence (5 dances with Miss Strong; Charlie danced 2).
- Miss Daisy Strong met Lawrence on Devil's Dyke (April), shower of rain, umbrella.
- Lawrence: medium height, very fair, blue eyes, pink-and-white complexion, soft penetrating voice, hard to be rid of.
- Pier: meets Cyril Paxton ("Where's Charlie?"). Lawrence introduced as "a sort of acquaintance."
- Cyril: "I knew that I should meet you on the pier."
- Cyril: investing in Eries, "bull on Eries"; "going for the gloves" to win/lose all. Emigration next week.
- Daisy: "marry... punting on the Stock Exchange." Charlie = Charlotte Wentworth.
- Trumpit Gold Mine mentioned as earlier loss.
- Daisy kisses Cyril.

### Ch II. Overheard in the Train
- Cyril buys first-class ticket; Gladstone bag (new, brown).
- Evening paper: "ROBBERY OF THE DUCHESS OF DATCHET'S DIAMONDS!"
- Value £250,000. Duchess travelled Windsor → Paddington. Servant Stephen Eversleigh carried leather despatch-box. Bank: Bartlett's Bank. Box empty at Grosvenor Square.
- Cyril notices man through glass partition: Lawrence (with German-American).
- Cyril listens via opened frame: Lawrence and "German-American" (the Baron) discuss theft. Eversleigh short-sighted; spectacles; detective camera copied spectacle case; trick at Windsor booking office; rug swap of despatch-boxes.
- Lawrence: "Simplicity... soul of all true art."

### Ch III. The Diamonds
- Train to Brighton. Cyril and Lawrence in refreshment room; Lawrence offers drink; Cyril refuses.
- Cyril's Gladstone bag won't open; contains a ring, tiara, necklaces: the Datchet diamonds.
- Realises he took Lawrence's bag by mistake.
- Amsterdam Necklace (~£100,000); Datchet Tiara; Begum's Brooch; Banee's Bracelet.
- Cyril decides to keep diamonds; hides them in Gladstone within evening paper.

### Ch IV. Miss Wentworth's Rudeness
- Daisy waiting at pier gates.
- Cyril: "I'm going for the gloves"—claims he'll make a fortune; secretive.
- Daisy: "Whither thou goest..." (Ruth); proposes marriage within a month.
- Charlie (Charlotte Wentworth): 30, writer ("Fashions"), 500 a year, pince-nez, sarcastic; she and Daisy share a house (Medina Villas).
- Charlie mocks; Cyril asks "Is it the Eries?"; Charlie: "marry a crossing-sweep" jibe; "honest?" insult; Cyril storms out.
- Daisy: "Cyril, you are an honest man."

### Ch V. In the Bodega
- Cyril in Bodega with whisky; Lawrence and Baron confront: "What was the colour of your Gladstone bag, eh?"
- Cyril lies: "black bag, seven or eight years old."
- Baron: tall, thin, black overcoat, large top hat, vulture nose, rolling mouth, no chin.
- Ireland (detective, "John Ireland") at bar: hints knows diamonds; "lifer" if caught with them.
- Ireland: "Lawrence" not his name; Cyril feigns innocence.

### Ch VI. The Adventures of a Night
- Cyril shadowed on West Street. Leaves Gladstone bag with hotel manager (Treadwater).
- Man in smoking-room interrogates Cyril about room number.
- Night: someone tries to pick lock; Cyril unlocks/bolts door; then burglar on ladder at window; Cyril fires revolver. Ladder left behind; lantern shattered.

### Ch VII. The Datchet Diamonds Are Placed in Safe Custody
- Morning: manager questions him.
- Cyril takes diamonds to Chancery Lane Deposit Company safe (rented earlier); journey by Pullman.
- Shadow in cab, ostentatious back; Cyril calls guard/constable.
- Jostled at London Bridge by two men trying to pick pockets; a countryman pretends to be clumsy.
- Newspapers: Datchet collection valued ~£500,000 by some.

### Ch VIII. In the Moment of His Success
- Cyril broke; Eries down; at bars; "sell diamonds? nonsense."
- Returns to Brighton; manager reports man claiming Cyril sent him for bag (sending Medina Villas).
- Evening paper City article: Trumpit Gold Mine shares boomed to £10.
- Cyril had bought 10,000 Trumpit shares earlier; they were unsaleable; now valued ~£100,000.
- Cyril seized from behind near hotel, chloroformed into a cab.

### Ch IX. A Proposal of Marriage
- Daisy waits on pier 20 min late; quarrel with Charlie (friends parted in anger).
- Lawrence meets her on pier: says he saw Cyril in town at Criterion bar, staying in town tonight.
- Lawrence proposes to Daisy ("ask you to be my wife"). Daisy: "I am engaged to Mr. Paxton."
- Daisy back home: Charlie teases; Daisy weeps; "Mr. Lawrence has dared to make me a proposal."

### Ch X. Cyril's Friend
- Mr. Franklyn (Cyril's lawyer/friend): ~40, grey-streaked black hair, grey-black eyes.
- Shares: Trumpit Gold shares £12 10s (were 2d); Franklyn holds 10,000 in strongbox.
- Daisy relieved; Franklyn goes to Makell's Hotel.

### Ch XI. John Ireland's Warrant
- Franklyn at hotel; manager says Cyril out.
- Ireland (detective) stops Franklyn: "Because I've a warrant for his arrest"—robbery of Duchess of Datchet's diamonds.
- Ireland bets Franklyn £100 at evens that Cyril has guilty knowledge.
- Ireland shows ring Cyril dropped from handkerchief outside Makell's (picked up by Ireland's man).
- Ireland orders Constable George Hollier to tail Franklyn.

### Ch XII. A Woman Roused
- Daisy at Medina Villas; Hollier at door.
- Franklyn tells Daisy & Charlie: Ireland suspects Cyril of possessing diamonds; Charlie: Cyril had talked of "quarter of a million at one coup."
- Daisy fierce: calls Charlie and Franklyn "cravens."
- Daisy leaves with Charlie and Franklyn to Makell's; Hollier follows.

### Ch XIII. The Detective and the Lady
- Ireland at Makell's office; clerk; manager Treadwater.
- Search warrant; strong-room; Gladstone bag found (shirts, underclothing, no jewels).
- Treadwater: Cyril took valuables to London.
- Ireland: "My man picked up the ring... that was the last he saw of Mr. Paxton."
- Daisy bursts in: furious at Ireland; "You wretched spy!" Ireland leaves man behind.
- Ireland on steps; Daisy follows.
- Bill Cooper (ragged, billycock) accosts Ireland: offers to betray "Tom the Toff" and "the Baron" for £50 (from Daisy) plus Ireland's money; Cooper says Paxton is captive; "they've took him to a crib."
- Ireland takes Cooper, Daisy into cab to police station; Charlie and Franklyn follow.

### Ch XIV. Among Thieves
- Cyril wakes bound hand and foot in a forge-like room (raftered, smoky, blacksmith's furnace).
- Captor: "Skittles," sinister, pail of water, slaps him.
- Baron arrives: long black coat, top hat; revolver; chloroform cloth recalled.
- Skittles/Baron torture: "Ready! Fire!" shots near ears.
- Lawrence arrives with two men; reveals he took diamonds (as Hargraves/"The Toff"); says Cyril took Lawrence's bag by mistake; Lawrence's proposal to Daisy mentioned: "what I so longed for already was your own."

### Ch XV. Put to the Question
- Lawrence's interrogation: demands location of Datchet diamonds; Cyril refuses.
- Lawrence: "Give us authority... you'll remain our prisoner."
- Threat: "tortures of the Spanish Inquisition."
- Lawrence orders branding iron marked "thief."

### Ch XVI. A Modern Instance of an Ancient Practice
- Skittles heats branding-iron; burns Cyril's shoulder; Cyril breaks ropes at wrists.
- Cyril butts Skittles, brains him with iron; takes Baron's revolver; Baron collapses (head wound).
- Lawrence whistles; Cyril's revolver empty (Lawrence knew).
- Cyril strikes Lawrence (head); fight; Cyril strikes lamp, setting fire.
- Cyril flees into pantry cupboard, bolted in by a man; window too small.
- Shouts "Help! Murder!" — echo "Hollo!" from distance.

### Ch XVII. The Most Dangerous Foe of All
- Gang members outside argue; flee in fly leaving Skittles, Baron, Lawrence inside.
- House burning; Cyril trapped; smoke.
- Cyril writes will on notepaper: "I give and bequeath all that I have in the world to my dear love, Daisy Strong... God bless her!—CYRIL PAXTON."

### Ch XVIII. The Last of the Datchet Diamonds
- Ireland, Cooper, sergeant, constables drive Downs; fly captured; villains arrested.
- House fire seen; Cooper: "they been and set it afire."
- Daisy finds hand at window; will falls out; she rescues Cyril.
- Weeks later, Cyril wakes; Daisy weeps.
- Cyril confesses to Daisy and police; diamonds retrieved from Chancery Lane safe; returned to Duchess.
- Trial: Lawrence (Reginald Hargraves, alias Arthur Lawrence, "The Toff") and Baron (Isaac Bergstein): each 20 years penal servitude; others shorter. Cyril testifies as Crown witness; Cooper also testifies.

### Ch XIX. A Woman's Logic
- Cyril realises Trumpit shares; invests in consols; vows no more gambling.
- Cyril and Daisy married quietly at a Brighton church.
- Daisy's "feminine logic" in quarrel after marriage; Cyril's concession: "God grant that I may never again be led into such temptation!"
